title: How ChatGPT Sales Plugin At DocuSign (DOCU) Has Changed Its Investment Story
detail:
How ChatGPT Sales Plugin At DocuSign (DOCU) Has Changed Its Investment Story
Al Bentley

DOCU
CRM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

DocuSign recently released its plugin for ChatGPT for Sales, letting sales teams pull signed terms, renewal deadlines, and commitments directly from DocuSign and connected CRMs like Salesforce to prepare renewals, generate contracts, and kick off Legal reviews inside the same conversation.

The plugin is powered by DocuSign's Model Context Protocol server. It feeds agreement intelligence and preset workflows into the tools sales reps already use, tightening the link between contract data and day-to-day selling activity.

We will look at how DocuSign's investment narrative intersects with this agreement intelligence plugin that surfaces contract terms inside ChatGPT.

See how DocuSign's agreement intelligence push compares with other AI driven software plays by reviewing our curated list of 43 profitable AI stocks that aren't just burning cash.

DocuSign Investment Narrative Recap

To own DocuSign, you need to believe the firm can turn its eSignature foothold into a broader intelligent agreement platform with steady, profitable compounding. According to rcb9, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the key swing factor is Intelligent Agreement Management, because core eSignature looks mature and ARR growth guidance is in the high single digits.

The ChatGPT for Sales plugin fits that belief but does not radically change the near term picture on its own. The more immediate catalyst still sits with IAM reaching the guided share of ARR and holding a non GAAP operating margin above 30%, while the main risk is IAM underperforming targets that underpin those mid single digit constant currency growth assumptions.

The new DocuSign plugin for ChatGPT for Sales is tightly linked to that IAM story. It pushes agreement intelligence directly into sales and legal workflows, connecting signed terms, renewal dates, and CRM data so that renewal briefs and contracts can be generated inside the same conversation rather than in disconnected tools.

This kind of usage is what rcb9 argues needs to happen for IAM to move from roughly one tenth of ARR toward the guided higher mix over time. Execution risk stays real, because revenue growth is forecast around 7.7% per year and cannot lean only on eSignature, but operational wins like this plugin are the practical test of whether IAM adoption can support the earnings growth that analysts currently expect to be above 20% a year.

According to rcb9's calculations, DocuSign reaches a fair value of $60.99 if revenue grows at 7% annually and the business ultimately maintains a 15% GAAP net margin, with that level of profitability supported by a declining share count as buybacks first offset and then exceed stock-based compensation.

title: Salesforce vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Software Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Salesforce vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Software Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool

CRM
PLTR
BRZE
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) and Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) represent two distinct ways to play the artificial intelligence boom. Which software provider offers the most compelling path for your portfolio over the next three years?

Salesforce provides a massive cloud platform for managing customer relationships, while Palantir builds operating systems that integrate disparate data for decision-making. Investors compare them because both are aggressively integrating generative AI into enterprise workflows to drive efficiency for global businesses.

The case for Salesforce

Salesforce provides customer relationship management (CRM) tools to businesses through its Agentforce 360 platform. The company is currently focused on deploying autonomous AI agents that can handle sales and service tasks without constant human oversight for its more than 10,000 customers. In its latest annual report, it also highlighted its expansive partner network and recent acquisitions like Braze (NASDAQ:BRZE) to bolster its data management and AI offerings.

In the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, revenue reached $43.9 billion, which is an 11.2% increase over the previous twelve-month period. Net income for this time frame was $9.7 billion, demonstrating the company's ability to maintain high profitability while transitioning to new AI products. This growth highlights the steady adoption of cloud-based tech stocks that focus on enterprise efficiency and customer retention.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.3x, suggesting the company maintains a conservative level of borrowing relative to its equity. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to liabilities, was 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow reached $14.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented 23.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Palantir Technologies

Palantir Technologies builds software platforms that allow organizations to integrate massive amounts of data with AI models for real-time decision-making. The company serves both government agencies and commercial enterprises, recently announcing a partnership with AmeriLife Group to apply AI in the insurance distribution market. Its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) is a core driver of its current strategy as more businesses look to move beyond simple chatbots toward operational AI tools.

title: How Risky Is Adobe Stock After Its Long Slide?
detail:
How Risky Is Adobe Stock After Its Long Slide?
Trefis Team

Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

Adobe (ADBE) stock has lost 30.4% over the past year, while the S&P 500 returned 11.0%. With shares trading at 12.3 times earnings against 21.5 for the S&P 500, buyers may see the risk as priced in. That assumption holds only if Adobe stock falls no more than the market in a sell-off. Adobe's sales would also need to keep growing while the company gives away free versions of its apps. So how has Adobe stock held up when the market fell?

How Far Has Adobe Stock Fallen In Market Shocks?

Adobe stock has fallen further than the S&P 500 in market shocks, on average. It has sometimes taken years to recover. Across 15 shocks since mid-2007, Adobe fell 21.4% on average against 15.8% for the S&P 500. Its steepest fall came in the 2008-2009 financial crisis. Adobe lost 63% then, while the index lost 53%.

From its low in a typical shock, Adobe took a median of 2.3 months to regain its earlier peak. Two recoveries ran far longer. Adobe needed 50.0 months after the 2008-2009 crisis, and 29.3 months after the 2010 eurozone debt crisis.

Adobe has not yet climbed back to its close of February 19, 2025, the day the 2025 tariff shock began.

Adobe's latest close is still 50.5% below that level, more than a year and a half later. If Adobe is a big part of your savings, that loss could take years to win back. In a free 30-minute review, our partner advisory firm can show you ways to limit your loss if the stock falls further and to sell with a smaller tax bill. Book the free review.

How Fast Is Adobe Growing Now?

Adobe's sales reached $26.0 billion in the four quarters to August 28, 2026, up 12.0% from a year earlier. That beats the 10.7% growth of the twelve months before. Adobe's sales are holding up while it courts free users. Digital Media, its largest business, generated $17.6 billion of Adobe's $23.8 billion in sales during fiscal 2025.

Adobe's operating margin has slipped slightly, coming in at 35.7% over the last four quarters against 36.2% a year earlier. The software maker also carries little debt. Its debt equals 7.6% of its market value, against 20.3% for the S&P 500.

Adobe's Backlog Is Growing More Slowly Than Its Sales

In fiscal Q3 2026, Adobe's subscription revenue grew 14% from a year earlier. Its backlog of signed contracts not yet counted as sales grew only 8%, to $22.16 billion. Management said on the September 10 call that this reflects its push to win new users through free versions of its apps. Adobe plans to turn those users into paying subscribers at a later stage.

title: Is ServiceNow A Better Buy Than Atlassian Now?

Is ServiceNow A Better Buy Than Atlassian Now?

Our Nov 18 look at Atlassian found the stock fell 6.0% on Tuesday, Nov 17, while the S&P 500 lost 1.0%. The company had no news that day. Yet 57 of the 62 other application software companies we track fell too. For that story, see What Explains The Move In Atlassian Stock?

The next question is which fallen software stock is the better buy now, Atlassian or ServiceNow. Our read is ServiceNow, on the numbers below. Both stocks fell because investors now pay less for each dollar of sales. Their sales did not slow much.

Atlassian closed at $135.05 on Wednesday, Nov 18. That is 9.2% below its price a year earlier. ServiceNow closed at $90.59, down 44.6% over the same year. The SPDR S&P 500 fund rose 10.6% in that time.

A common view is that AI agents could replace software sold per user, or per seat. This article does not test that view. It splits each fall into two parts. One is growth in sales. The other is the price investors pay for those sales.

Did sales growth slow at Atlassian and ServiceNow?

Not by much. Atlassian's revenue grew 23.7% in the quarter to Sept 30. A year earlier, it grew 20.6%. ServiceNow's revenue grew 20.5%, against 21.8% a year before.

Over the last four quarters, ServiceNow's sales rose 21.8% from a year earlier. Yet its market value fell 44.9% over the past year. Atlassian's sales rose 26.6%, while its market value fell 11.3%. Market value also counts changes in share count, so it differs a little from the stock moves above.

ServiceNow kept growing its sales, but its stock still fell 44.6% in a year. If a fall like that has hit a stock you own, you can plan how to protect what is left. Our partner advisory firm offers a free 30-minute strategy review covering a floor under losses and a lower-tax way out. Map your exit options.

How much less are investors paying for each dollar of sales?

Price-to-sales is a company's market value divided by its sales over the last four quarters. A year ago, ServiceNow traded at 13.5 times sales. On Wednesday it traded at 6.1 times. That multiple fell 54.7%.

Atlassian's multiple fell from 7.2 times sales to 5.0 times. That is a drop of 30.0%. For both companies, the lower multiple explains the whole fall in market value. Sales growth pushed the other way.

The reported numbers do not show why buyers chose to pay less. The same thing happened at two other large software makers, Workday and Salesforce. Their latest figures run through the July quarter, two months earlier. The table below shows growth and price-to-sales for all four.

However, we have identified three blue-chip stocks with a favorable Zacks Rank that have provided strong guidance and carry solid price upside potential in the near term. These are: Cisco Systems Inc. CSCO, UnitedHealth Group Inc. UNH and Salesforce Inc. CRM.

Cisco Systems Inc.

Cisco's prospects are benefiting from broad demand across networking, security and collaboration. AI infrastructure orders, integrated silicon and an end-of-support refresh opportunity support a multi-year networking cycle, while newer security products and Splunk's recovery broaden the growth base. CSCO also retains operating leverage and continues to return cash to shareholders.

Strong Guidance

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, CSCO expects revenues between $18 billion and $18.2 billion. Non-GAAP earnings are projected at $1.34-$1.36 per share, with a non-GAAP gross margin of 65-66% and an operating margin of 36-37%. For fiscal 2027, management projects revenues of $74.8-$75.8 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $5.47-$5.53 per share.

Solid Estimate Revisions

Cisco has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 18.4% and 20.3%, respectively, for the current year (ending July 2027). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year's earnings has improved 0.8% over the last seven days. CSCO has a current dividend yield of 1.77%.

It has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 9.2% and 9.4%, respectively, for the next year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for next year's earnings has improved 0.9% over the last seven days.

Robust Price Upside

The short-term average price target of brokerage firms represents an increase of 34% from the last closing price of $97.18. The brokerage target price is currently in the range of $109-$150. This indicates a maximum upside of 54.4% and no downside.

UnitedHealth Group Inc.

UnitedHealth Group's diversified operations and disciplined pricing support its growth prospects. Optum remains a key earnings driver, aided by integrated care, AI-enabled solutions and pharmacy services. Commercial fee-based membership gains and a healthy sales pipeline provide further opportunities.
